content: This reaction is reversible. Bromophenol blue is utilized as a color marker to monitor the progress of agarose gel electrophoresis and polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. Due to its slight negative charge at moderate pH levels, bromophenol blue migrates in the same direction as DNA or proteins within a gel. The migration rate of bromophenol blue depends on the gel density and the composition of the buffer. In a standard 1% agarose gel prepared with TAE or TBE buffer, bromophenol blue migrates at a rate equivalent to that of a DNA fragment approximately 500 base pairs in length. Xylene cyanol and Orange G can also serve this purpose. The molecular weight of bromophenol blue is approximately 670 Daltons (or grams per mole). Bromophenol blue is also employed as a dye. At neutral pH, the dye absorbs red light most strongly and transmits blue light, resulting in a blue appearance in solution. At low pH, the dye absorbs ultraviolet and blue light most strongly, giving it a yellow appearance in solution. When dissolved in water without pH adjustment, bromophenol blue exhibits a characteristic green-red color, which corresponds to the middle of its pH transition range. Bromophenol blue is frequently used in introductory laboratory courses to stain proteins on wet-mount slides.
